carousel.cover_headline:
When Monsoon Hits,
Who Pays for Malaysia's
Food Insecurity?

slides.label: THE PATTERN
slides.headline: Malaysia's food supply is vulnerable when monsoon arrives.
slides.insight: Seasonal disruption puts pressure on what reaches your plate.

slides.label: WHO FEELS IT
slides.headline: Families at the market notice it first: less choice, higher prices.
slides.insight: Food insecurity is not abstract — it shows up at dinner.

slides.label: THE REAL COST
slides.headline: **Someone** always pays — usually the household, not the system.
slides.insight: When supply drops, prices rise and budgets shrink.

slides.label: IN MALAYSIA
slides.headline: A country that grows less locally depends more on what comes in.
slides.insight: Less local supply means more exposure to seasonal shocks.

slides.label: TRY THIS WEEK
slides.headline: Buy an extra local vegetable and store it this week.
slides.insight: A small buffer at home is your own food security.

carousel.caption:
When monsoon hits, who pays for Malaysia's food insecurity?

Seasonal disruptions affect what lands on your table and what it costs.
Local production gaps mean families absorb the pressure when supply drops.
What do you do when market prices suddenly spike?

Sources: Focus Malaysia, 2026
